problem:
Consider the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\sqrt{y+3x+2}-3.
$$

 
The general solution to this equation can be expressed in the form

$$
g(x,y)=x+C,
$$

where $C$ is a constant. What is $g(x,y)?$

feedback.problem:
Consider the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\sqrt{x+y}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+y)}-1.
$$

 
The general solution to this equation can be expressed in the form

$$
g(x,y)=\frac{x}{2}+C,
$$

where $C$ is a constant. What is $g(x,y)?$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we make the substitution

$$
z=x+y.
$$

Differentiating $z(x)$ using the chain rule, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}=1+\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,⟹\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}-1.
$$

Therefore, the original equation can be written in terms of $z$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}-1 & =\frac{\sqrt{z}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡z}-1\end{aligned}
$$

Expressing this equation in the form ${z}^{′}(x)=f(z)$ gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\sqrt{z}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡z}.
$$

This differential equation is separable. So, we separate the variables and integrate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡z}{\sqrt{z}}\,\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x} & =1 \\ \int \frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡z}{\sqrt{z}}\,\text{d}z & =\int \,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

Using integration by parts on the left side,

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡z & \,⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{z} \\ {v}^{′}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{z}} & \,⟹\,v=2\sqrt{z}\end{aligned}
$$

we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡z}{\sqrt{z}}\,\text{d}z & =\int \,\text{d}x \\ 2\sqrt{z}\operatorname{ln}⁡z-2\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{z}}\,\text{d}z & =\int \,\text{d}x \\ 2\sqrt{z}\operatorname{ln}⁡z-4\sqrt{z} & =x+K \\ 2\sqrt{z}(\operatorname{ln}⁡z-2) & =x+K \\ \sqrt{z}(\operatorname{ln}⁡z-2) & =\frac{x}{2}+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=\frac{K}{2}.$

Finally, we write the equation in terms of $y$ and $x$ using our original substitution, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{x+y}\,(\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+y)-2) & =\frac{x}{2}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $g(x,y)=\sqrt{x+y}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+y)-2).$
